Issue No.1 9.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.

Witness may not have called the police but all those facts as coming in the cross examination do not go to show that witness was not present at the place of accident or had not seen the incidence.
Important to note PW2 Akhilesh is the complainant before the police and it is on his complaint criminal case was registered.
Evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from the certified copy of site plan prepared in the criminal case of accident in question i.e. FIR No.50/2020 of PS Babugarh, District Hapur.

Thus, in view of the evidence of PW2 and other material available on record this Tribunal is of considered view that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no. UP-32CN-3700.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 14.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
MACT No.125/2020 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 6  MALIK Date: 2024.05.07  16:14:09 +0530  COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Rajkamal Sharma.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by MACT No.125/2020 Digitally signed by Page 7 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:14:15 +0530 the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be Shikha Sharma And Ors vs Arif And Ors on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118139827/
5 added."

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

Insurance company in this case has taken the plea that it is not liable to pay the amount of compensation on account of breach of terms of insurance policy as the special permit regarding the offending vehicle no.UP-32CN-3700 was not available at the time of accident as such special permit was issued for 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020 and it was issued from the office of RTO on 02.37 p.m.
As such at the time when the accident occurred at 08.00 a.m. of 12.02.2020, bus was being plied without any special permit.

31. To substantiate this fact insurance company has examined witness Narender Singh (R3W1) who is investigator of New India Assurance Company Limited and stated the above said facts in his affidavit and stated that he got the information under RTI Act which is Ex.R3W1/1, permit Shikha Sharma And Ors vs Arif And Ors on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118139827/

sentences.text: Another witness examined is R3W2 Naveen Kumar from RTO Meerut who also stated that a special permit in respect of bus no.UP-32CN-3700 was issued in the name of Khalid s/o Haji Iqbal Hamim from 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020 for route of special permit of Meerut to Ghaziabad and return.

Report is Ex.R3W2/2.
32.
Important in this context also to refer the evidence of owner/ respondent no.2 Khalid who examined himself as R2W1 and stated that no accident has taken place from his bus no.UP-32CN-3700.
Moreover the said bus was insured with respondent no.3 company under insurance policy Ex.RW2/1.

Witness further says that at the time of alleged accident the bus was having a valid permit no.71/99 effective from 19.04.2019 to 18.04.2024 which is Ex.RW2/2 and he also applied for a special permit Mark A for 12.02.2020 for a route from Meerut to Ghaziabad for a marriage party.
33.

It be noted that insurer under the M.V. Act is entitled to raise MACT No.125/2020 Digitally signed by SHAILENDER Page 14 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:15:15 +0530 defences to counter the claim petition for compensation inter alia in terms of section 149(2) of M.V.
Act on the ground of breach of policy condition such as disqualification of driver, invalid or fake licence, transport vehicle being plied without permit etc.
It be noted in this regard insurance company in order to avoid its liability must establish defence raised and also establish the breach on the part of owner of the vehicle.
Obviously the onus of proving the breach of insurance policy terms is on the insurance company.
In that process the Tribunal is under duty to interpret the insurance policy conditions and also to consider whether there was a fundamental breach of policy in terms of Section 149(2) of the Act.

34. In the present case the whole endeavor of insurance company is to prove that special permit for period from 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020, was granted only at 02.37 p.m. of 12.02.2020 whereas accident took place in the morning at 08.00 a.m. of 12.02.2020, therefore there was no special permit at the time of accident.

Such plea does not however establish breach much less to say fundamental breach of insurance policy terms, firstly because the evidence of R3W1 Narender Singh is based on the RTI information whereas it is matter of practice and also came in the evidence of R3W2, the official from RTO Meerut that for applying the special permit, as per practice it is to be applied online and therefore even if in the process of making all formalities, the special permit was issued late in the afternoon but the report of Secretary RTO Ex.R3W2/2 clearly shows that permit was from 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020.
There is no specific time mentioned in the permit.

Moreover even for the time being special permit is ignored, it came in the evidence of R2W1 Khalid (owner of offending vehicle) that offending vehicle had a valid permit which was effective from 19.04.2019 to 18.04.2024 and is Ex.RW2/2.

There is no cross examination MACT No.125/2020 Page 15 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.07 16:15:22 +0530 of R2W1 on this aspect nor that fact has been disputed even in the evidence led on behalf of insurance.

In such circumstance when offending vehicle was having a valid permit as well as special permit for 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020, there was to the opinion of the Tribunal no fundamental breach of insurance policy terms, therefore the insurance company is liable to pay the amount of compensation.

opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of pleadings following issues were framed on 18.12.2021 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle No. UP-32CN-3700 on 12.02.2018 at about 08:00 am near Shahpur Jatt Dharamkanta GT Road, Hapur within the jurisdiction of PS Babugarh, Hapur in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh.Rajkamal Sharma?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
Thus, in view of the evidence of PW2 and other material available on record this Tribunal is of considered view that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no. UP-32CN-3700.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
MACT No.125/2020 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 6  MALIK Date: 2024.05.07  16:14:09 +0530  COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and MACT No.125/2020
Obviously the onus of proving the breach of insurance policy terms is on the insurance company.
In that process the Tribunal is under duty to interpret the insurance policy conditions and also to consider whether there was a fundamental breach of policy in terms of Section 149(2) of the Act.
34. In the present case the whole endeavor of insurance company is to prove that special permit for period from 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020, was granted only at 02.37 p.m. of 12.02.2020 whereas accident took place in the morning at 08.00 a.m. of 12.02.2020, therefore there was no special permit at the time of accident.
Such plea does not however establish breach much less to say fundamental breach of insurance policy terms, firstly because the evidence of R3W1 Narender Singh is based on the RTI information whereas it is matter of practice and also came in the evidence of R3W2, the official from RTO Meerut that for applying the special permit, as per practice it is to be applied online and therefore even if in the process of making all formalities, the special permit was issued late in the afternoon but the report of Secretary RTO Ex.R3W2/2 clearly shows that permit was from 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020.
In such circumstance when offending vehicle was having a valid permit as well as special permit for 12.02.2020 to 14.02.2020, there was to the opinion of the Tribunal no fundamental breach of insurance policy terms, therefore the insurance company is liable to pay the amount of compensation.
